articleBody:
Before installers arrive with your new kitchen cabinets, a little upfront work keeps the project on schedule and protects your home. Run through this checklist to make sure your space is fully prepared.

- [ ] Measure entryways and hallways — Clear a wide path from the front door to the kitchen so large cabinet boxes fit through without scraping trim or walls.
- [ ] Empty every existing cabinet completely — Clear out cookware, dry goods, and dishware ahead of time so workers can start immediately without handling your belongings.
- [ ] Confirm stud locations and utility marks — Mark plumbing lines, electrical wiring, and gas connections on a sketch so fasteners never strike hidden pipes or cables.
- [ ] Check local permit requirements — Verify with your municipal building department whether your cabinet project or related utility updates need an active permit.
- [ ] Inspect finished flooring for level — Find the highest spot on your subfloor or tile to help the installer establish accurate base cabinet reference lines.
- [ ] Set aside a dry, clean staging room — Clear space in a garage or adjoining living area where delivered cabinet boxes can sit protected from dirt and moisture.
- [ ] Remove fragile wall decor in nearby rooms — Take down mirrors and pictures hanging on the opposite side of shared walls to prevent vibration damage during fastening.
- [ ] Secure pets and establish a safe zone — Keep pets and children away from the kitchen work zone to ensure a safe, efficient workspace throughout the job.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items two to three days before installation begins. If you run into uneven framing or have questions about electrical or plumbing clearance, Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC provides hands-on guidance. Reach out at 303-505-0866 to schedule your installation.
